full_judgment: 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule, in brief, are: The petitioner is a limited company incorporated under the Companies Act. Mrs. Madlena D Rozario (since deceased), wife of Ketu Rozario purchased the land appertaining to CS Plot No. 177 of mouza Begunbari, PS Tejgaon, Dhaka measuring an area of 1.25 acres of land from the CS recorded owners by a registered deed of sale dated 12-6-1950. The name of Mrs. Rozario was duly recorded both in SA and RS khatiansin respect of that land. The Government by an order dated 3-3-1952 requisitioned the land under section 30f the East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 (hereinafter referred to as the Act) and included the same in LA Case No. 16 of 1959-60 for the purpose of cutting earth for the Railway Department. The land was subsequently de-requisitioned, released and restored to Mrs Madlena D Rozario by issuing a notice under Rule 10(2) of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Rules, 1948 issued under the joint signatures of the Additional Land Acquisition Collector, Dhaka and the Additional District Magistrate, Dhaka Despite the release and restoration of possession of the land to the original owner, the same was included in the list of enemy property in the Tejgaon Police Station VP Case No. 566 of 1968 at the behest of certain interested quarters. For proper utilisation and management including power to sell off the land, Mrs. Rozario executed and registered a general power of attorney in favour of her son, Jacob Rozario and one Edward Purification on 14-1-1986. The attorneys of the original owner entered into a contract with Md Saifur Rahman Khan on 14-1-1986 to sell 0.18 acre of land and delivered possession thereof to him. Since the attorneys refused to execute and register the deed of sale, Md Saifur Rahman Khan instituted a suit for specific performance of contract being Title Suit No. 84 of 1988 in the 2nd Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka. The suit was decreed by judgment and decree dated 15-8-1988 (Annexure-E). During pendency of the suit, the then Martial Law Government issued Martial Law Order (MLO) No. 128 dated 13-5-1986 which was published in the official Gazette on 20-5-1986 cancelling all previous letters, orders as if they had never been issued in respect of the lands acquired by erstwhile Government of East Pakistan under LA Case No. 66 of 1957-1958. LA Case No. 16/1959-1960 was also included in the schedule to that MLO for the construction of Dhaka Tongi Diversion Road. By the MLO all the previous letters, orders and instruments were cancelled and re-vested the properties described in the schedule of the MLO to the Government. The legal heirs of Mrs Rozario in compliance with the decree executed a deed of sale dated 30-9-1989 in favour of the petitioner's vendor, Md Saifur Rahman Khan. Thereafter, the attorneys of the original owner also executed a deed of exchange and transferred more land in favour of the petitioner's vendor. In this way the petitioner's vendor became owner of 0.19 acre of land appertaining to CS Plot No. 177 of Begunbari Mouza, Tejgaon, Dhaka. Since the land was released in favour of Mrs. Rozario, she made a series of applications to the different authorities including the vested property authority for release and restoration of the disputed land. Accordingly, the land was released from the list of vested property and ultimately, it was restored to the original owner. Respondent No.6, the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka filed a suit being Title Suit No. 28 of 1992 in the 3rd Court of Additional Assistant Judge, Dhaka seeking declaration that the decree dated 15-8-1988 (Annexure-E) passed in Title Suit No. 84 of 1988 and the deed of exchange dated 3-6-1989 were illegal and inoperative, and also sought for recovery of khas possession. The plaint of the suit was rejected on a contested hearing by judgment and order dated 16-5-1996 against which the Government did not prefer any appeal. Respondent No.2 issued letter dated 18-7-1993 and allotted 5 kathas of land which is the petitioner's land treating the same as industrial plot No. 30 in favour of respondent No.8, Habib Hotel International Limited but did not hand over possession thereof. The petitioner purchased 5 kathas of land from Md Saifur Rahman Khan on payment of valuable consideration and got registration of the deed of sale bearing No. 1752 dated 2-5-1996. The name of the petitioner was mutated in respect of that 5 kathas of land in Miscellaneous Case No. 144 of 1998 dated 6-10-1998. The Government recently carried out a survey in which the name of the petitioner was duly recorded. After a long lapse of 10 years of allotment, respondent No.2 executed and registered a deed of lease dated 9-10-2002 in favour of respondent No.8 but could not deliver possession thereof. When the respondents threatened to dispossess the petitioner from his purchased land, he filed a suit being Title Suit No. 189 of 2003 in the 2nd Court of the Assistant Judge, Dhaka for permanent injunction. On an application filed by the petitioner, the trial Court passed an ad-interim order directing the parties to maintain status quo which was made absolute on 21-6-2003. On an appeal by the respondents, the order of status quo was stayed on 28-6-2003. in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 175 of 2003 respondent No. 2 issued a letter dated 26-5-2003 directing the Executive Engineer, Public Works Division 3, Segunbagicha, Dhaka to arrange for handing over possession of the disputed land to respondent No.8. The respondents unilaterally obtained an order on 3-6-2003 setting aside the mutation and deleting the petitioner's name from the record of right. When it came to the knowledge of the petitioner, it filed an appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 65 of 2003 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Dhaka and obtained an order of stay on 22-6-2003.
